A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ChildMandarin dataset and benchmark study. Their text, tables, figures, and equations support comparison. All 11 pages of v1 and 13 pages of v3 were inspected; v3 adds Appendices A and B, while v1 ends with references.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset statistics, ASR experiments in Tables 4, 6, and 7, and speaker-verification results in Table 8.

after.justification: v3 retains original ASR and speaker-verification experiments and adds demographic performance breakdowns, error-type results, and utterance-level comparisons.

M1.justification: The same ASR and speaker-verification architectures, training approaches, and decoding procedures remain. Shortened baseline descriptions, revised parameter-count reporting, and newly disclosed hyperparameters do not establish an algorithm or architecture change.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ASR and speaker verification on the same 41.25-hour Mandarin corpus from 397 children aged 3–5. The new age/gender breakdowns and utterance examples analyze existing coverage rather than introducing another dataset, population, or task.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain unchanged: Transformer, Conformer, Paraformer, Wav2vec 2.0, HuBERT, CW, and Whisper for ASR, and x-vector, ECAPA-TDNN, and ResNet-TDNN for speaker verification. v1's speaker-verification Table 8 becomes Table 9 in v3 without comparator changes.

E3.justification: Table 5 revises Wav2vec 2.0 base/large parameter counts from 368M/1,215M to 97M/318M and HuBERT counts from 369M/1,216M to 97M/319M. These are reported model-size revisions, without evidence of checkpoint substitution or rerunning. v3 also adds groupwise CER and error-component evaluation. Dataset splits, decoding beam size, and SV trial design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a substantial diagnostic layer absent from v1: Section 4.1.5 compares CW performance across six age/gender groups and decomposes errors into substitutions, deletions, and insertions. Appendix B adds five transcription comparisons illustrating corrections and residual errors after fine-tuning.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added subgroup results and Figure 5 continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Table 7 changes CW's zero-shot/fine-tuned CER from 19.36%/14.39% to 18.05%/13.66%, without explaining the revision. v3 additionally reports subgroup error profiles and five utterance-level outcomes. The other aggregate ASR scores and all speaker-verification scores remain unchanged, preserving the principal model rankings.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces original theoretical results or proofs. v3 removes the standard CER formula and its explanation without changing the metric; the EER and DCF definitions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain the Mandarin dataset for children aged 3–5, its demographic coverage, and its demonstrated utility for ASR and speaker verification. Fine-tuning benefits and proposed applications remain the same. The added analyses support these existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: Section 4.1.5 adds interpretations involving age, gender, possible pitch/articulation variability, and targeted adaptation. Appendix B discusses residual difficulty with longer or complex utterances. Existing limitations remain unchanged. The new statement that CER decreases with age overgeneralizes Figure 5/Table 8, where four-year-olds outperform five-year-olds within each gender.

D1.justification: Appendix A supplies previously absent model-specific batch sizes, learning rates, warmup settings, epoch counts, SV learning-rate schedules, hardware, and approximate runtime. v3 also provides a dataset access link, specifies character-level annotation, and documents parental consent, compensation, anonymization, and access restrictions. These substantially expand reproducibility and collection documentation without establishing changed experiments.

R1.justification: The Dong and Xu (2020) CIF citation and reference are removed when the Paraformer description is shortened. The remaining related-work coverage and positioning around scarce Mandarin resources for young children are substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the statistics discussion, condenses baseline explanations, updates authors and affiliations, and adds an analysis subsection, Ethics Statement, and appendices. Most existing prose and section order remain intact. Section 4.1.2 introduces an incorrect reference to Table 8 for scratch-training results, which remain in Table 4.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands visual reporting with paired demographic CER bars, an error-type comparison table, three configuration tables, and color-highlighted transcription comparisons in Figure B.1. Table 2 is compacted and relocated, and existing figures and tables are reflowed. The original demographic plots and benchmark-table designs are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses important documentation omissions for a dataset paper: it provides an explicit access reference, model-specific training configurations, and consent, compensation, and anonymization information absent from v1. These substantially improve reproducibility and scrutiny of data collection, while the new diagnostics make recognition errors easier to inspect. The overstated age trend, unexplained CW score revisions, and incorrect table reference temper but do not outweigh these gains.
